# react-useanimations The official React component for [useAnimations](https://useanimations.com):
**300 free animated icons with hover, click and loop interactions built in.** [![npm version](https://img.shields.io/npm/v/react-useanimations?style=flat-square&color=7c5cff)](https://www.npmjs.com/package/react-useanimations) [![npm downloads](https://img.shields.io/npm/dm/react-useanimations?style=flat-square&color=7c5cff)](https://www.npmjs.com/package/react-useanimations) [![dependencies](https://img.shields.io/badge/dependencies-0-7c5cff?style=flat-square)](https://www.npmjs.com/package/react-useanimations?activeTab=dependencies) [![types](https://img.shields.io/npm/types/react-useanimations?style=flat-square&color=7c5cff)](src/index.tsx) [![license](https://img.shields.io/npm/l/react-useanimations?style=flat-square&color=7c5cff)](LICENSE) [**Browse all icons →**](https://useanimations.com/#icons)  ·  [Documentation](https://useanimations.com/documentation)  ·  [shadcn/ui](https://useanimations.com/documentation#shadcn)  ·  [Upgrading from v2](#upgrading-from-v2)
## Why useAnimations - **Every icon already knows how to move.** Loaders loop, menus toggle, the trash can opens on hover, social icons play while you point at them. You pick the icon; the interaction comes with it. - **Tiny, zero dependencies.** A built-in 8 kB (gzipped) player renders the icons as SVG. An icon is 2 kB on median, and your bundle includes only the icons you import. - **Styled like text.** Icons follow `currentColor`, so `className="text-blue-600"`, Tailwind and plain CSS just work. - **Accessible and calm.** Decorative by default, labelled when you pass `aria-label`, played by keyboard focus too, and still when the user prefers reduced motion. - **Ready for modern React.** React 18 and 19, StrictMode, Next.js App Router and server rendering, no `dynamic(..., { ssr: false })` needed. - **Typed and searchable.** Full TypeScript types; hover an icon import in your editor to see its title, keywords, interaction and preview. - **shadcn/ui registry.** Add any icon to your project as a ready-made component with one command. - **Bring your own Lottie.** Your own animations play through the same player and props. ## Quick start ```bash npm install react-useanimations ``` ```jsx import UseAnimations from 'react-useanimations'; import github from 'react-useanimations/lib/github'; export default function App() { return ; } ``` Point at the icon: it loops while hovered, exactly like on [useanimations.com](https://useanimations.com). Every icon is its own module, so only what you import ends up in your bundle. Several icons can also be imported from one place; production builds still include only the icons you use: ```javascript import { github, heart, menu } from 'react-useanimations/icons'; ``` Prefer `react-useanimations/lib/` when your dev server or test runner doesn't tree-shake, since `react-useanimations/icons` loads every icon there. The component is also available as the named exports `UseAnimations` and `UseAnimation` (the name used by the [shadcn registry](https://useanimations.com/documentation#shadcn)). ### shadcn/ui Every icon is also in a [shadcn registry](https://useanimations.com/r/registry.json). The CLI adds a ready-made component and installs `react-useanimations`: ```bash npx shadcn@latest add https://useanimations.com/r/checkmark.json ``` ```tsx import { AnimatedCheckmark } from '@/components/animations/checkmark'; ; ``` ## Interactions Each icon comes with the interaction it has on [useanimations.com](https://useanimations.com). Pass `interaction` to pick another one. | Interaction | What it does | For example | | :------------- | :----------------------------------------------- | :-------------------- | | `hover-replay` | plays once on hover | `arrowRight`, `zap` | | `click-replay` | replays on every click | `download`, `send` | | `click-toggle` | toggles between two states on click | `menu`, `heart` | | `loop` | plays continuously | `loading`, `activity` | | `hover` | plays forward on hover, backward on leave | `trash`, `settings` | | `hover-loop` | loops while hovered, finishes the cycle on leave | `github`, `twitter` | ```jsx ``` Hover animations also play on keyboard focus (when the icon or its wrapper is focusable) and ignore taps on touch screens. Looping icons pause while they are scrolled out of view. ## Props ```jsx ``` | Prop | Default | Definition | | :---------- | :--------------: | :---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | | animation | / | icon imported from `react-useanimations/lib/`, or `{ animationData, interaction }` for your own Lottie JSON | | size | `24` | width and height; numbers are pixels, strings are any CSS length (e.g. `'1.5em'`) | | strokeColor | `'currentColor'` | color of the icon's strokes; by default the icon follows the text color | | fillColor | `strokeColor` | color of the icon's filled parts (e.g. a liked heart) | | interaction | per icon | `'loop'`, `'click-toggle'`, `'click-replay'`, `'hover'`, `'hover-loop'` or `'hover-replay'` | | active | / | for `click-toggle` icons: `true` shows the end state; controlled, so set it in `onClick` (clicks don't toggle it) | | autoplay | per icon | `true` for `loop` icons, unless reduced motion is preferred | | loop | per icon | `true` for `loop` and `hover-loop` icons | | speed | `1` | playback speed (1 is normal speed) | | render | / | render prop for a custom wrapper, see [A real button](#a-real-button) | Any other prop (`className`, `aria-label`, `onClick`, `onMouseEnter`, …) is passed to the wrapper ``. Your event handlers run before the animation's; call `event.preventDefault()` to skip the animation. ## Recipes ### Colors and stroke width Icons follow the text color by default, so `className="text-blue-600"` or `style={{ color: 'red' }}` recolors them. The built-in rule has zero specificity, so your own CSS always wins: ```jsx // Tailwind ``` ```css /* plain CSS: */ .icon path { stroke-width: 3; } ``` Some icons cut a gap into themselves (the slash in `visibility`, `microphone`, `video`, `volume` and `notification`, the check in `download`, the ring around `notification3`'s badge). The gap takes the page background: white on light pages and dark on pages with `color-scheme: dark`. On other backgrounds, set it with the `--ua-knockout` CSS variable, e.g. `body { --ua-knockout: #0f172a; }`. ### Controlled toggle ```jsx import { useState } from 'react'; import UseAnimations from 'react-useanimations'; import menu from 'react-useanimations/lib/menu'; export const MenuButton = () => { const [open, setOpen] = useState(false); return ( setOpen(!open)} /> ); }; ``` ### A real button For clickable icons, put an interactive element around the icon with the `render` prop, so it is focusable and works with the keyboard: ```jsx import heart from 'react-useanimations/lib/heart'; export const LikeButton = () => ( console.log('liked')} render={(eventProps, animationProps) => ( )} /> ); ``` `eventProps` holds the `onClick`, `onMouseEnter`, `onMouseLeave`, `onPointerEnter`, `onFocus` and `onBlur` handlers for your interactive element and `animationProps` holds the animation itself, which you spread on a `` inside it. ### Your own Lottie animation ```jsx import animationData from './my-animation.json'; ; ``` The player supports what icon animations use: shape layers, precompositions, null layers and parenting, paths, rectangles, ellipses, strokes, fills, trim paths, masks, keyframes with easing, holds and motion paths, and the `loopOut()` and `wiggle()` expressions. Gradients, solid, text and image layers, effects, mattes and other expressions are not rendered; the console warns about them once per animation. If the player can't draw an animation, that animation stops and the error is logged once; other icons keep playing. ### Next.js and other SSR frameworks The component is marked `'use client'` and renders the animation only in the browser, so it can be rendered from server components without `dynamic(..., { ssr: false })`. Functions such as `onClick` or `render` can't be passed from a server component: render the icon inside a client component for those. Icons inside a shadow root are styled there too. ## Accessibility and motion - Icons are decorative by default (`aria-hidden`).
